      India-Pakistan ceasefire helps support risk sentiment
    

  
 (Updates to morning US trade)
    By Chuck Mikolajczak
       NEW YORK, May 12 (Reuters) - The dollar surged on Monday
as the United States and China reached a deal to temporarily cut
reciprocal tariffs, easing concerns a trade war between the
world's two biggest economies could lead to a global recession.
     The U.S. will reduce extra tariffs it imposed on Chinese
imports in April to 30% from 145% and Chinese duties on U.S.
imports will fall to 10% from 125%, effective for 90 days. The
de-escalation surpassed investor expectations, with many
expecting an introductory round of talks with few, if any,
agreements.
     
  
       "It's 90 days and so this basically buys some more time,
I sort of think the U.S. blinked," said Marc Chandler, chief
market strategist at Bannockburn Global Forex in New York.
  
       "I'm not a big fan of the tariffs in the first place, but
once they were in place, the U.S. seemed to back down without
getting much in exchange. That is, we stopped with our
reciprocal tariffs on China and so they unwind their reciprocal
tariffs on us, but we're still back at square one." 
  
         The dollar index <=USD>, which measures the greenback
against a basket of currencies including the yen and the euro,
rose 1.2% to 101.58, with the euro <EUR=> down 1.17% at $1.1115
and on track for its biggest one-day decline of the year.
    The risk-on mood propelled U.S. stocks sharply higher, with
the S&P 500 up more than 2%, and weighed on safe-haven
currencies, with the dollar up 1.91% against the Japanese yen
<JPY=> to 148.12 after reaching 148.59, its highest level since
April 3.
         Against the Swiss franc <CHF>, the dollar rose 1.4% to
0.843 after reaching 0.8475, its highest since April 10.
  
         Sterling <GBP=> weakened 0.8% to $1.3198 and was on
track for its biggest daily drop since April 7.
     While the greenback has strengthened for three straight
weeks on growing optimism over potential trade deals, the dollar
is still down 2.2% since April 2, when Trump announced sweeping
tariffs as his uneven rollout of policies and exemptions shook
confidence in U.S. assets.
         The focus this week will also be on U.S. Consumer Price
Index (CPI) figures on Tuesday and on April retail sales due on
Thursday for indications of how the global trade conflict has
impacted the economy and expectations for further interest rate
cuts by the U.S. Federal Reserve. 
  
         Traders on Monday dialed back on rate cut expectations
by the 
    Fed
     and 
    European Central Bank
     as economic prospects improved after the Sino-U.S. trade
deal. Markets now see the first cut of at least 25 basis points
(bps) from the Fed as likely to come at the central bank's
September meeting, compared with the July view last week. 
  
     
  
       The Chinese yuan <CNH=> strengthened 0.64% against the
greenback to 7.194 per dollar. Meanwhile, geopolitical tensions
also appeared to ease over the weekend, further supporting risk
sentiment.
    India and Pakistan announced a ceasefire following four days
of fighting between the nuclear powers which had rattled
markets.
    Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said he was ready to
meet Russian leader Vladimir Putin in Turkey on Thursday for
direct talks. That would be the first negotiations between the
two countries since the early months of Russia's 2022 invasion.

headline: FOREX-Dólar sobe após trégua entre China e EUA aliviar temores sobre crescimento

Por Chuck Mikolajczak
       NOVA YORK, 12 Mai (Reuters) - O dólar subia nesta
segunda-feira, uma vez que os Estados Unidos e a China chegaram
a um acordo para reduzir temporariamente as tarifas recíprocas,
diminuindo as preocupações de que uma guerra comercial entre as
duas maiores economias do mundo poderia levar a uma recessão
global.
    Os EUA reduzirão as tarifas extras que impuseram sobre as
importações chinesas em abril de 145% para 30%, e as tarifas
chinesas sobre as importações dos EUA cairão de 125% para 10%,
com vigência de 90 dias. A redução das tensões superou as
expectativas dos investidores, pois muitos esperavam uma rodada
introdutória de negociações com poucos ou nenhum acordo.
     
    "São 90 dias e, portanto, isso basicamente dá mais algum
tempo", disse Marc Chandler, estrategista-chefe de mercado da
Bannockburn Global Forex, em Nova York.
    "Em primeiro lugar, não sou um grande fã das tarifas, mas
uma vez que elas foram implementadas, os EUA pareceram recuar
sem receber muito em troca. Ou seja, paramos com nossas tarifas
recíprocas sobre a China e, portanto, eles diminuíram suas
tarifas recíprocas sobre nós, mas ainda estamos de volta à
estaca zero."
    O índice do dólar <=USD>, que mede o dólar em relação a uma
cesta de moedas, incluindo o iene e o euro, subia 1,2%, para
101,58, com o euro <EUR=> caindo 1,17%, a US$1,1115, e a caminho
de sua maior queda diária do ano.
    O dólar subia 1,91% em relação ao iene japonês <JPY=> para
148,12, depois de atingir 148,59, seu nível mais alto desde 3 de
abril.
    Em relação ao franco suíço <CHF>, o dólar ganhava 1,4%, para
0,843, depois de atingir 0,8475, seu nível mais alto desde 10 de
abril. A libra <GBP=> enfraquecia 0,8%, para US$1,3198, e estava
a caminho de sua maior queda diária desde 7 de abril.
    Embora o dólar tenha se fortalecido por três semanas
consecutivas com o crescente otimismo em relação a possíveis
acordos comerciais, a moeda norte-americana ainda acumula queda
de 2,2% desde 2 de abril, quando Trump anunciou tarifas
abrangentes, já que sua implementação irregular de políticas e
isenções abalou a confiança nos ativos dos EUA.
    Nesta semana, o foco também estará nos números do índice de
Preços ao consumidor dos EUA na terça-feira, e nas vendas no
varejo de abril na quinta-feira, com os investidores buscando
obter indicações de como o conflito comercial global afetou a
economia e as expectativas de novos cortes na taxa de juros pelo
Federal Reserve.

Li e Danilo Masoni)

headline: MORNING BID AMERICAS-Re-set, surge and hold
news:
By Mike Dolan
       LONDON, May 13 (Reuters) - What matters in U.S. and
global markets today
By Mike Dolan, Editor-At-Large, Financial Industry and Financial
Markets
      
With the dramatic re-set of U.S.-China tariffs on Monday, the
market completed the hair-raising round-trip it has been on over
the past six weeks of trade angst. Punch-drunk investors are now
assessing whether anything in the real economy broke in the
process.   
In today's column, I explore whether the sudden easing of China
tariffs may actually be related to an economic theory that has
long been prized by American conservatives: the Laffer Curve.
    Now onto all of today's market news.
     
    Today's Market Minute
  
* A White House executive order said on Monday that the U.S.
would cut the "de minimis" tariff on China shipments to 54% from
120%, with a flat fee of $100 to remain starting from May 14.
* U.S. President Donald Trump arrived in Saudi Arabia on Tuesday
to start a four-day swing through the Gulf region, focusing more
on economic deals than security crises ranging from war in Gaza
to the threat of escalation over Iran's nuclear program.
* Apple’s success rests on the iPhone, which helped turn the
company from a niche player in the personal computer industry
into one of the world’s largest companies. Much of that was due
to its supply chain in China. Now geopolitical tensions and
trade wars are calling that dependence into question.
* The move by the United States and China to reduce import
tariffs on each other and negotiate has been broadly welcomed by
markets, but the de-escalation will do very little to restore
the trade in energy commodities. Check out why in the latest
piece from Reuters' columnist Clyde Russell.
* A split is emerging between the Federal Reserve and other
major central banks as they try to assess the economic impact of
the rapidly shifting trade war. The Fed's cautious stance runs
the risk of leaving Chair Jerome Powell and his team behind the
curve once again. Read the latest from Reuters' columnist Jamie
McGeever.
     
    Re-set, surge and hold
  
    The S&P 500 <.SPX>, Nasdaq <.IXIC> and Dow Jones <.DJI>
indexes all boasted gains of 3-5% on Monday, their biggest
single-day percentage gains since April 9. The S&P is now back
within 1% of where it started the year, breaking above its
200-day moving average for the first time since late March.
    Stock futures <Esc1> dialed back a touch on Tuesday, but
retained most of their recent gains.  
    Following the positive China trade news, the dollar <.DXY>
hit its highest point in a month before falling back a bit
today. China's offshore yuan <CNH=> outpaced it to briefly notch
its best levels since November's U.S. election.
After Monday's agreement between the two biggest economies, the
White House followed up with an executive order saying America
would also cut the "de minimis" tariff on China shipments to 54%
from 120%.
    In the meantime, U.S. Treasury yields <US10YT=RR> are back
near mid-April levels as Federal Reserve rate expectations have
been pegged back to just two cuts this year.    
    Back to square one? Well, not quite.
    U.S. tariffs have come off the mountain top, and the
investor relief is palpable. Goldman Sachs cut back its U.S.
recession chances to 35% from 45%. They are the first major
brokerage to do so.
BlackRock CEO <BLK.N> Larry Fink says tens of trillions of
dollars of financial firepower is sitting idle in cash amid
trade war worries and uncertainty over the U.S. economy, where
deficits are beginning to spook investors.
    And the April 2 moves are still only paused for three
months, with negotiations ongoing. The overall effective U.S.
tariff rate at this point is still almost five times what it was
at the start of the year, even if it has almost halved from last
week. 
    Indeed, the effective tariff rate is currently around 13%
according to the Fitch credit rating firm, so it's still the
highest since World War Two.
    While everyone waits and watches, economic stress tests are
unfolding, with April's consumer price report due on Tuesday and
retail and industrial numbers for the month out later in the
week.
    Headline annual inflation is expected to have remained
steady at 2.4% last month.
However, there was a deep intake of breath before the report,
following news that U.S. new-vehicle prices surged in April, a
sign that Trump's auto-tariff measures at least are already
rippling through the car market. The average price consumers
paid, after discounts and promotions, rose 2.5% from March, more
than double the typical 1.1% increase over those two months in
recent years, Cox Automotive's Kelley Blue Book showed.
    And there were further signs of trepidation among households
and companies ahead of the tariff sweep.
Top U.S. bank lending officers reported weaker demand from
businesses and consumers for many types of credit during the
first three months of the year, according to a Federal Reserve
report released on Monday, reversing a short-lived surge in loan
demand the previous quarter.
    Elsewhere, stocks around the world remained buoyant on the
tariff detente - nudging higher on most bourses in Asia and
Europe. Positive British wage data and German ZEW investor
sentiment readings helped.
Make sure to check out my column today, where I look a little
deeper at the effectiveness of the tariff hikes, why they were
pulled back from the brink and why budget and government revenue
considerations may now be top of mind.
     
    Chart of the day 
  
    U.S. consumer price inflation for April is due for release
on Tuesday, as households may be starting to experience the
impact of the April 2 import tariff hikes. Due to a variety of
lags related to existing contract expirations and producers
absorbing some of the hit, economists think today's report will
paint an incomplete picture. It could be several months before
the full impact is revealed. 
    As per Monday's U.S.-China re-set, the tariff target is
changing all the time. What is clearer is the wide gap between
inflation trends in the U.S. and China since the pandemic, with
Beijing reporting this week that CPI inflation in April is still
in negative territory. That speaks both to the difference in
domestic demand in both countries and also relative
competitiveness.
     
    Today's events to watch
  
    * U.S. April consumer price report (8:30EDT)
    * New York Federal Reserve issues Q1 Household Debt and
Credit Report (10:00EDT) 
    * Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey and Chief Economist
Huw Pill speak
    * European Union finance ministers meet in Brussels, with
European Central Bank Vice President Luis de Guindos
    * U.S. President Donald Trump visits Middle East on
three-country tour to Saudi Arabia, Qatar and United Arab
Emirates (to May 16)
    * NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte travels to Ankara ahead
of informal meeting of NATO Ministers in Antalya on May 14-15

headline: FOREX-Dollar eases after cooler than expected CPI
news:
* 
      US CPI slightly below estimates
    

        * 
      Tariffs still likely to impact inflation
    

        * 
      Several brokerages cut recession outlook
    

  
 (Updates to morning US trading)
    By Chuck Mikolajczak
       NEW YORK, May 13 (Reuters) - The dollar retreated on
Tuesday, pulling back from sharp gains in the prior session
after a reading on inflation was less than market expectations.
        The Labor 
    Department 
    said the consumer price index (CPI) increased 0.2% last
month, under expectations of economists polled by Reuters for a
0.3% gain, after dipping 0.1% in March.
  
        Still, inflation is likely to pick up steam in the
coming months as U.S. 
    tariffs
     lift the cost of imported goods. 
  
        "While the headline number for inflation was better than
expected, there are indicators that tariffs have already pushed
prices higher," said Brian Jacobsen, chief economist at Annex
Wealth Management in Menomonee Falls, Wisconsin.
  
        "Turning down the temperature of tariffs is good as the
price effects would start seeping into the consumer basket
pretty quickly. The 
    trade reset
     with China might mean the Fed can go back to business as
usual and gradually resume cutting rates later this year."
  
        The dollar index <=USD>, which measures the greenback
against a basket of currencies including the yen and the
euro, fell 0.36% to 101.36, with the euro <EUR=> up 0.5% at
$1.1142.
    The greenback rallied more than 1% in the prior session on
optimism a tariff deal between the United States and China could
cool a trade war between the world's two largest economies that
raised the risk of a global recession.
    The dollar is still more than 2% below its April 2 level,
when U.S. President Donald Trump announced tariffs and prompted
overseas investors to reduce their exposure to U.S. stocks and
bonds. 
    Against the Japanese yen <JPY=>, the dollar weakened 0.45%
to 147.78, after rallying more than 2% in the prior session as
the risk-on mood dented the appetite for safe-haven assets.
    The greenback weakened 0.47% to 0.841 against the Swiss
franc <CHF=> after climbing 1.6% on Monday.
        The dollar <CNH=> edged up 0.01% to 7.199 versus the
offshore Chinese yuan, after falling to a six-month low of
7.1779. 
        The curtailment of U.S.-China trade tensions has led
market participants to dial back odds of a recession, along with
expectations for the timing and magnitude of rate cuts from the
Federal Reserve this year. 
        Major brokerages, including Goldman Sachs, J.P. Morgan
and Barclays have 
    recently scaled back
     their U.S. recession forecasts and their view of Fed policy
easing. 
  
        A rate cut of at least 25 basis points (bps) is now seen
as likely at the central bank's September meeting, compared with
the prior view for a cut at the July meeting, according to LSEG
data. About 51 bps of cuts are now being priced in for 2025.
  
        Sterling <GBP=> strengthened 0.43% to $1.3229.
    Among cryptocurrencies, bitcoin <BTC=> gained 0.99% to
$103,699.57 after hitting a high of $105,716,07 on Monday, a
3-1/2 month high. Ethereum <ETH=> rose 2.44% to $2,547.01.

headline: FOREX-Dólar recua após dados de inflação abaixo do esperado nos EUA
news:
Por Chuck Mikolajczak
       NOVA YORK, 13 Mai (Reuters) - O dólar recuava nesta
terça-feira, devolvendo parte dos ganhos acentuados da sessão
anterior, depois que uma leitura sobre a inflação ao consumidor
nos Estados Unidos ficou abaixo das expectativas de analistas.
    O Departamento do Trabalho informou que seu índice de preços
ao consumidor subiu 0,2% no mês passado, abaixo das expectativas
de economistas consultados pela Reuters, que esperavam um ganho
de 0,3%, depois de ter caído 0,1% em março.
    Ainda assim, é provável que a inflação ganhe força nos
próximos meses, uma vez que as tarifas dos EUA aumentam o custo
dos produtos importados.
    "Embora o número principal da inflação tenha sido melhor do
que o esperado, há indicadores de que as tarifas já aumentaram
os preços", disse Brian Jacobsen, economista-chefe da Annex
Wealth Management.
    "Diminuir a temperatura das tarifas é bom, pois os efeitos
dos preços começariam a se infiltrar na cesta de consumo muito
rapidamente. O reinício do comércio com a China pode significar
que o Fed pode voltar a agir como de costume e retomar
gradualmente os cortes de juros ainda neste ano."
    O índice do dólar <=USD> -- que mede o desempenho da moeda
norte-americana frente a uma cesta de seis divisas -- caía
0,48%, a 101,230.
    O dólar subiu mais de 1% na sessão anterior, com o otimismo
de que um acordo tarifário entre os EUA e a China poderia
esfriar uma guerra comercial entre as duas maiores economias do
mundo, que vinha elevando o risco de uma recessão global.
    O dólar ainda está mais de 2% abaixo de seu nível de 2 de
abril, quando o presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, anunciou as
tarifas e levou os investidores estrangeiros a reduzir sua
exposição a ações e títulos dos EUA.
    O dólar tinha queda de 0,4% em relação ao iene <JPY=>, a

headline: BUZZ-COMMENT-Resurgent option prices demonstrate lingering FX fears
news:
May 14 (Reuters) - A sharp drop in FX option implied volatility on
Monday reflected improved risk sentiment following reduced tariffs from
U.S.-China trade talks. However, the subsequent rebound in the volatility risk
premium from this forward looking FX derivative underscores the underlying
anxiety. 
    The bulk of G10 FX option 1-12-month expiry term structures saw their
implied volatilities hit new setback lows, with many completely reversing the
gains seen after the initial April 2 tariff announcements. However, there was
renewed demand on Tuesday, despite the improved risk sentiment holding and the
stock market volatility index <.VIX> trading below 20.0. 
    The options market may have been over sold, allowing hedgers to take
advantage of the much lower levels and subsequent reward versus risk. There's
been a renewed surge in implied volatility across all currency pairs and
maturity dates in early London trading on Wednesday as news broke of May 5 talks
between South Korea and the U.S. involving Forex. 
    This renewed demand took benchmark 1-month EUR/USD implied volatility to
8.15 from 7.6 on Wednesday, having based at 7.0 on Monday. Its directional risk
premium, as shown by risk reversal options, had warned of the simmering upside
risks to spot. 
    USD/JPY 1-month implied volatility is up from 10.0 to 10.7 on Wednesday from
a 9.5 setback low on Monday, with its directional risk premium still flagging
downside spot vulnerability.

headline: BUZZ-FX options wrap - FX volatility risks are far from over
news:
The big sell-off in FX volatility and USD put risk premiums at the start of the
week appear to have been overdone, with a recovery underway even before
Wednesday's resurgence. 
    A recovery for risk and the USD after news of the weekend's successful trade
negotiations between the U.S. and China saw implied volatility in many of the
major currency pairs and across all maturity dates retrace more, if not all of
the post-April 2 tariff announcement gains. Implied volatility eventually found
a floor late Monday/early Tuesday, but met strong and renewed demand. 
    News of a meeting between the U.S. and South Korea concerning forex, which
took place on May 5, reached the market on Wednesday. The reaction was to sell
the USD and buy implied volatility. The USD/JPY drop and implied volatility
gains took the benchmark 1-month expiry from 10.0 to 10.7, having based in the
mid 9s prior to that. Risk reversals regained premium for downside over topside
strikes - 1-month expiry from 1.5 to 2.1 JPY calls over JPY puts. 
    EUR/USD 1-month implied volatility reached 8.25 from 7.6 on Wednesday - it
had based around 7.0 previously. EUR/USD risk reversals maintain a strong
topside over downside strike risk premium, which continues to flag what the
market believes is still the most vulnerable direction for spot and implied
volatility gains.

from 5-year highs in early April to 1-year lows.

headline: BUZZ-FX options wrap - FX hedging opportunities abound
news:
FX hedging opportunities have become more attractive as broad FX option implied
volatility retreats from the sharp spike seen after the April 2 U.S. tariff
announcement, which briefly pushed vols to long-term highs. The subsequent
pullback has made hedging costs cheaper, prompting renewed interest from market
participants.
    While the broader trade tariff situation is far from resolved, interim
90-day reprieves — with global trading partners until July 8 and with China now
extended to August 10 — have helped restore a degree of calm. As volatility has
eased, the U.S. dollar has recovered from its earlier lows against several major
currencies, leading to a decline in overall implied volatility.
    However, lower premium levels mean that less realised volatility is needed
to cover option costs and generate returns — enhancing the attractiveness of FX
options as a hedging tool. Notably, premiums on USD puts (the right to sell the
dollar) have been more resilient, underscoring the market's uncertainty over the
USD's future direction.
    USD/JPY holds a strong correlation with risk and broader USD trends, making
it a key barometer for FX option activity. It's no surprise that USD/JPY options
saw the sharpest response following renewed fears surrounding Asian FX after
Wednesday's headlines regarding U.S.–South Korea trade and FX discussions.
    While implied volatility rose broadly on Wednesday, USD/JPY extended those
gains on Thursday. Benchmark 1-month USD/JPY implied volatility jumped from a
post-trade-reprieve low of 9.5% to 11.3%. Risk reversal options are now showing
a renewed surge in demand for USD/JPY downside protection, particularly after
the 3-month expiry tenor—which notably extends beyond the U.S.–China tariff
truce.

headline: BUZZ-FX options wrap - Cautious consolidation with weak USD outlook
news:
Recent price action across FX markets points to cautious consolidation, with a
continued bearish bias for the USD in several currency pairs.
    Implied volatility had completed its retracement from the April spike -
triggered by the initial U.S. tariff announcement - following progress in
U.S.-China trade talks. However, fresh demand emerged Tuesday as value-seeking
traders and hedgers took advantage of cheaper premiums to cover against future
volatility.
    USD/JPY implied volatility posted the biggest bounce in a move that also saw
a strong recovery in the premium for downside over upside strikes as measured by
risk reversal contracts. One-month expiry implied volatility regained almost 2.0
to 11.3, while 1-month and 3-month expiry risk reversals recovered around 1.0 to
2.45 and 2.65 respectively for JPY calls over puts. Next week's potential trade
talks between Japan and the U.S. are the near term USD/JPY risk, while the post
August 10 China tariff extension has also attracted some hedging flows.
    In Asia, USD/KRW dropped sharply after mid-week headlines touted early May
discussions between the U.S. and South Korea on foreign exchange - reviving
concerns about currency manipulation as a trade negotiation tool. The move
triggered a spike in USD/KRW option volatility, further boosting demand for JPY
hedges.
    EUR/USD remains range-bound near 1.1200, with huge strike expiries anchoring
price action amid a lack of fresh drivers. One-month implied volatility bounced
midweek to 8.3 before settling near 7.6, off Tuesday's low of 7.1. Risk
reversals retain a solid topside over downside strike premium, and ongoing
demand for EUR calls/USD puts, show a market still hedging the risk of further
EUR/USD gains. 
    It's a similar situation in GBP/USD, where implied volatility holds above
setback lows and risk reversals maintain a 5-year high premium for topside over
downside strikes.

headline: 《全球汇市》美元下跌，受美国信评遭下调和贸易紧张局势拖累
news:
* 
      交易员权衡美国前景，美元兑日圆跌至10日低点
    

        * 
      美国贸易紧张局势继续酝酿，英国金融时报报道与欧盟解冻
    

        * 
      贝森特警告对谈判缺乏"善意"国家的关税将回到4月2日水平
    

        * 
      聚焦英国与欧盟会谈
    

  
       路透东京5月19日 - 美元兑多种货币周一下跌，兑避险货币日圆
跌至10日低点，因市场消化美国政府信用评级被意外下调的影响，而且贸
易摩擦疑虑也影响了市场信心。
    
    穆迪（Moody's）上周五下调美国的主权信用评级，从"Aaa"下调一级
至"Aa1"，因担心美国债务的可持续性，成为最后一家摘除美国顶级AAA信
评的三大信评机构。
    
    这一消息导致美元兑其他主要货币走低；而在此之前，美元已连续四
周上涨，原因是对美国贸易协议的乐观情绪升温，而且美国与中国的紧张
关系缓和，也缓解了对全球经济衰退的担忧。

    "对政府来说，这个消息出现在一个尴尬的时刻，因为政府正试图在 
7 月初之前让国会通过一项预算。这进一步引发了对赤字、美国公债和美
元避风港地位的合理质疑，”法国兴业银行的外汇和利率企业研究主管Ke
nneth Broux说。
    
    他说：“今天的情况提醒我们美元的脆弱性。”
    
    美元兑日圆<JPY=EBS>周一最多下滑0.7%，报144.665日圆，为5月8日
以来低点，欧元兑美元<EUR=EBS>升0.73%，报1.1247美元。
    
    穆迪调降美国评级，中国外交部周一就此表示，美国应采取负责任的
政策和措施以维持国际金融、经济和财政系统的稳定性，并保护投资者利
益。[nL4S3RR0G9]
    
    美国财政部长斯科特-贝森特（Scott Bessent）周日在接受电视专访
时表示，贸易谈判缺乏"善意"的国家，总统特朗普将会以4月2日宣布的税
率对其征收关税。[nL6S3RQ05D]
    
    不过，英国金融时报报道称，美国已开始与欧盟进行认真的贸易谈判
，打破了长期以来的僵局，这为美国在本月稍早与英国签署框架协议后达
成更多交易带来了一些希望。
    
    特朗普此前表示，他与印度、日本和韩国也有可能达成交易，不过与
东京的谈判似乎因汽车关税问题而陷入僵局。

    "市场上对于各国达成交易的能力有着很强的自满情绪，"澳洲国民银
行(NAB)外汇策略主管Ray Attrill表示。"对于美国经济将会渡过难关的
信心很值得怀疑。"

    英镑兑美元<GBP=D3>上涨0.6%，至1.33595美元，交易商关注欧盟与
英国谈判的进展。
    
    英国周一料将与欧盟达成自英国脱欧以来最重要的关系重置协议，寻
求在贸易和防务方面进行更紧密的合作，以帮助经济增长并加强欧洲大陆
的安全。
    
    在赢得国会一个关键委员会的批准后，特朗普扫清了通过一项全面减
税法案的障碍，该法案将在未来十年导致美国增加约3万亿至5万亿美元的
债务。

    美元兑另一种避险货币瑞郎<CHF=EBS> 下跌0.45%，至0.83355瑞郎。
    
    澳新银行（ANZ）外汇研究主管Mahjabeen Zaman说："对美国经济增
长风险和美国政府政策议程的关注，可能使美国资产的避险地位受到质疑
。"。
    
    澳元兑美元<AUD=D3>上涨0.34%，至0.64255澳元，此前澳元连续三天
下跌，澳洲央行周二将宣布政策决定，市场普遍预期该央行将降息25个基

headline: FOREX-Dólar cai após rebaixamento do crédito dos EUA, tensões comerciais pesam
news:
Por Rocky Swift e Kevin Buckland e Lucy Raitano
       TÓQUIO, 19 Mai (Reuters) - O dólar caía em relação a uma
série de moedas nesta segunda-feira, atingindo uma mínima de dez
dias em relação ao iene, conforme os mercados digeriam um
inesperado rebaixamento da recomendação de crédito dos Estados
Unidos, enquanto as tensões comerciais também pesavam.
    A agência Moody's rebaixou na sexta-feira a classificação de
crédito dos Estados Unidos em um degrau, de "Aaa" para "Aa1",
sendo a última das principais agências de recomendação a
rebaixar o país, citando preocupações sobre sua crescente dívida
de US$36 trilhões.
    A notícia fez com que o dólar caísse em relação aos seus
principais rivais depois de quatro semanas consecutivas de
ganhos, quando foi impulsionado pelo aumento do otimismo em
relação aos acordos comerciais com os EUA e, em seguida, por um
redução na tensão das relações com a China, o que diminuiu os
temores de uma recessão global.
    "Isso ocorre em um momento difícil para o governo, que tenta
aprovar um orçamento no Congresso até o início de julho. Isso
levanta outras questões legítimas sobre o déficit, o status de
segurança dos Treasuries e do dólar", disse Kenneth Broux, chefe
de pesquisa corporativa para câmbio e taxas do Société Générale.
    "Hoje é um lembrete da fragilidade do dólar", disse ele.
    O dólar chegou a cair 0,7%, para 144,665 ienes <JPY=EBS> -
seu nível mais baixo vez desde 8 de maio, enquanto o euro
<EUR=EBS> subia 0,73%, a US$1,1247. O dólar ainda caía 0,45%,
para 0,83355 franco suíço <CHF=EBS>, outra moeda segura.
    A China pediu aos Estados Unidos nesta segunda-feira que
tomem medidas responsáveis para manter a estabilidade do sistema
financeiro e econômico internacional e proteger os interesses
dos investidores.
  ((Tradução Redação São Paulo))
    REUTERS CMO

news:
* 
      Dollar dips to ten-day low vs yen as traders weigh U.S.
outlook

      U.S. trade tensions simmer, FT reports thaw with EU
    

        * 
      Bessent warns of April 2 tariff levels for nations that

      UK-EU defence and trade ties 'reset'
    

  
 (Updates latest price moves, adds latest UK-EU trade talks

    By Rocky Swift, Kevin Buckland and Lucy Raitano
       TOKYO, May 19 (Reuters) - The U.S. dollar fell against a
range of currencies on Monday, slipping to a ten-day low versus
the safe-haven yen as markets digested a surprise downgrade of
the U.S. government's credit rating while trade tensions also
brought the mood down.
    Moody's cut the United States' top sovereign credit rating
by one notch on Friday, the last of the major ratings agencies
to downgrade the country, citing concerns about its growing $36
trillion debt pile.
        The news saw the dollar lose ground against its major
rivals following four straight winning weeks when it was boosted
by rising optimism for U.S. trade deals and then a thaw in
relations with China that eased fears of a global recession.
    "It looks like the dollar is facing a new round of short
building after Friday’s downgrade by Moody’s. S&P500 futures
down -1.2% and Treasuries are under pressure: it’s a textbook
'sell America' session in markets," said Francesco Pesole, FX
strategist at ING. 
        The greenback slipped as much as 0.7% to 144.665 yen
<JPY=EBS> - its lowest level since the first time since May 8 on
Monday, meanwhile the euro <EUR=EBS> was 0.73% higher at
$1.1247.
  
        Sterling <GBP=D3> added 0.79% to $1.33850 versus the
weaker dollar, rising to its highest level since April 30 as
Britain agreed the most 
    significant reset of defence and trade
     ties with the European Union since Brexit on Monday. 
  
        S&P 500 futures were off 1.1%, on track to underperform
European equities with the STOXX 600 <.STOXX> last down 0.6%,
while U.S 10-year treasuries rose 11.5bps to 4.5545%. 
  
    "It comes at an awkward time for the administration as it
tries to get a budget through Congress by early July. It raises
further legitimate questions over the deficit, safe haven status
of Treasuries and the dollar," said Kenneth Broux, head of
corporate research for FX and rates at Societe Generale. 
        "Today is a reminder of the fragility of the dollar," he
said. 
  
         
    China on Monday
     called on the United States to take responsible policy
measures to maintain the stability of the international
financial and economic system and safeguard the interests of
investors.
  
    It follows U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent saying in
television interviews on Sunday that President Donald Trump will
impose tariffs at the rate he threatened last month on trading
partners that do not negotiate in "good faith."
    However, a Financial Times report that the United States had
begun serious trade talks with the European Union, breaking a
long deadlock, offered some hope for additional deals after
Washington inked a framework agreement with Britain earlier this
month.
    Trump has previously said he has potential deals with India,
Japan and South Korea as well, although talks with Tokyo seem to
be stumbling over car tariffs.
    In the market, "there's a lot of complacency about the
ability to pull off deals," said Ray Attrill, head of FX
strategy at National Australia Bank.
    "Confidence that the U.S. economy is going to weather this
is very much open to question."
    Elsewhere, Trump cleared a hurdle towards passing a sweeping
tax cut bill that would add an estimated $3 trillion to $5
trillion to the nation's debt over the next decade, after
winning approval from a key congressional committee. 
    The dollar declined 0.41% to 0.833390 Swiss franc <CHF=EBS>,
another safe-haven currency. 
    "The focus on U.S. growth risks and the U.S.
administration's policy agenda may have put the U.S. safe-haven
status in question," said Mahjabeen Zaman, head of foreign
exchange research at ANZ.
        Australia's dollar <AUD=D3> was up 0.66% to $0.64460
following three days of declines ahead of Tuesday's Reserve Bank
of Australia policy announcement, with a quarter-point cut
widely expected.
  
    New Zealand's kiwi dollar rose 0.6% to $0.59145 <NZD=D3>.

headline: Рубль дорожает в преддверии телефонных переговоров Путина и Трампа
news:
МОСКВА, 19 мая (Рейтер) - Рубль закрепился в плюсе на
дневных торгах понедельника в преддверии сегодняшних телефонных
переговоров глав США и РФ, сам факт которых формально может
выступать поддержкой; также на его стороне постепенное
увеличение продаж экспортной выручки под приближающийся Единый
налоговый платеж. 
    В рублевых котировках доллара отражается и ослабление
американской валюты на форексе после понижения суверенного
кредитного рейтинга США.
    Биржевые котировки юань/рубль расчетами "завтра" к 15.15 МСК
находились вблизи отметки 11,10, рубль набирает 0,7%.
        Беспоставочные однодневные фьючерсные контракты на пары
юань/рубль, доллар/рубль, евро/рубль на Мосбирже котировались к
этому времени по 11,11, 80,65 и 90,69 соответственно, и рубль
набирает против юаня и доллара по 0,7%, против евро дорожает на
0,1%.
    Пара доллар/рубль <RUB=> котируется на форексе по 80,10,
рубль набирает 1,1%, согласно данным LSEG.
    Пара евро/рубль <EURRUB=> котируется на форексе по 90,30,
рубль набирает 0,1%.
    Президент США Дональд Трамп намерен созвониться с
президентом России Владимиром Путиным сегодня в 17.00 МСК, чтобы
обсудить прекращение конфликта в Украине, после чего  планирует
переговорить с украинским президентом Владимиром Зеленским и с
рядом глав стран-членов НАТО.
    Предстоящие переговоры Путина и Трампа могут подсветить
перспективы России при различных вариантах выхода из украинского
конфликта, чреватого для РФ новыми западными санкциями в случае
его продолжения.
    Рубль остается в числе лидеров рынка форекс по темпам роста
с начала 2025 года, котируется вблизи многомесячных максимумов и
показывает положительную динамику в текущем месяце, продолжая
подпитываться надеждами на урегулирование конфликта и
нормализацию отношений между Москвой и Вашингтоном. 
    "Общая геополитическая картина для РФ сохраняет возможности
для будущей нормализации отношений с США и достижения соглашений
по Украине", - полагает Владимир Евстифеев из банка Зенит. 
    "В моменте на ожиданиях деэскалации курс способен уходить
ниже 11,10 рубля за юань, но в более долгосрочной перспективе
потенциал ослабления рубля сохраняется", - говорится в
аналитическом обзоре банка Санкт-Петербург.
    В состав проходящего 28 мая Единого налогового платежа
входит и налог на добычу полезных ископаемых (НДПИ),
уплачиваемый значительной частью экспортных компаний. Экспортеры
обычно наращивают продажи инвалюты за рубли под расчеты с
бюджетом, что обычно оказывает поддержку российской валюте во
второй половине календарного месяца.
    Согласно оценке Рейтер, объем уплачиваемого в мае
апрельского НДПИ для нефтяного сырья может составить 550
миллиардов рублей против 634 миллиардов месяцем ранее.
    Локально на стороне российской валюты играет и ослабление
внутреннего спроса на инвалюту, в том числе с учетом сокращения
импортных закупок на фоне снижения интереса населения к тратам в
пользу роста рублевых сбережений из-за высокой ключевой ставки
ЦБР (21% годовых).
    На форексе валюта США значительно дешевеет после понижения
агентством Moody's суверенного кредитного рейтинга США. Индекс
доллара <=USD> снижается на 0,9% и оценивается в 100,22. В паре
с евро доллар теряет почти один процент, текущие котировки
евро/доллар <EUR=> - $1,1265.
    По мнению Евстифеева из Зенита, глобальное ослабление
доллара и стабилизация нефтяных цен остаются факторами поддержки
для рубля.
    На прошлой неделе базовые нефтяные сорта достигли максимумов
с конца апреля, но сегодня они дешевеют после китайской
статистики, отразившей замедление в апреле темпов промышленного
производства и розничных продаж в КНР, а также на фоне снижения
кредитного рейтинга США.
    Баррель Brent <LCOc1> сейчас стоит чуть дешевле $65, теряя в
цене 0,7% с начала понедельника.
    

 (Московское бюро)

headline: FOREX-El dólar cae tras rebaja de calificación crediticia de EEUU, lastrado por tensiones comerciales
news:
Por Rocky Swift, Kevin Buckland y Lucy Raitano
       TOKIO, 19 mayo (Reuters) - El dólar estadounidense caía
el lunes frente a varias divisas, alcanzando mínimos de diez
días frente al yen, mientras los mercados digerían la sorpresiva
rebaja de la calificación crediticia del Gobierno estadounidense
y las tensiones comerciales también deprimían el ánimo.
    * Moody's recortó el viernes en un escalón la calificación
crediticia soberana de Estados Unidos, la última de las
principales agencias de calificación en rebajar la nota del
país, citando la preocupación por su creciente deuda de 36
billones de dólares.
    * La noticia hizo que el dólar perdiera terreno frente a sus
principales rivales tras cuatro semanas consecutivas de
ganancias, en las que se vio impulsado por el creciente
optimismo en torno a los acuerdos comerciales de Estados Unidos
y, posteriormente, por una distensión en las relaciones con
China que alivió los temores a una recesión mundial.
    * El billete verde llegó a caer un 0,7% frente a la moneda
japonesa, a 144,665 yenes <JPY=EBS>, su nivel más bajo desde el
8 de mayo, mientras que el euro <EUR=EBS> subía un 0,73%, a
1,1247 dólares.
    * La libra esterlina <GBP=D3> subía un 0,79%, a 1,33850
dólares, alcanzando su nivel más alto desde el 30 de abril,
después de que Reino Unido acordó el lunes el reajuste más
significativo de sus lazos comerciales y de defensa con la Unión
Europea desde el Brexit.
    * Los futuros del S&P 500 bajaban un 1,1%, camino de
registrar un rendimiento inferior al de la renta variable
europea, con el STOXX 600 <.STOXX> bajando por última vez un
0,6%, mientras que el rendimiento de los bonos del Tesoro
estadounidense a 10 años subía 11,5 puntos básicos, a 4,5545%.
    * "Llega en un momento incómodo para el Gobierno, que
intenta aprobar un presupuesto en el Congreso a principios de
julio. Plantea más preguntas legítimas sobre el déficit, el
estatus de refugio seguro de los bonos del Tesoro y el dólar",
dijo Kenneth Broux, jefe de investigación corporativa de divisas
y tipos de Societe Generale.
    * China pidió el lunes a Estados Unidos que tome medidas
políticas responsables para mantener la estabilidad del sistema
financiero y económico internacional y salvaguardar los
intereses de los inversores.
    * El secretario del Tesoro de Estados Unidos, Scott Bessent,
dijo en entrevistas televisivas el domingo que el presidente
Donald Trump impondrá aranceles al ritmo que amenazó el mes
pasado a los socios comerciales que no negocien de "buena fe".
    * Sin embargo, un informe del Financial Times de que Estados
Unidos inició conversaciones comerciales serias con la Unión
Europea, rompiendo un largo estancamiento, ofreció cierta
esperanza de acuerdos adicionales después de que Washington
firmó un acuerdo marco con Reino Unido a principios de este mes.
    * Por otra parte, Trump superó un obstáculo para aprobar un
amplio proyecto de ley de recorte de impuestos que añadiría
entre 3 billones y 5 billones de dólares a la deuda del país
durante la próxima década, tras obtener la aprobación de un
comité clave del Congreso.
    * El dólar bajaba un 0,41% a 0,833390 francos suizos
<CHF=EBS>, otra divisa de refugio.

 (Reporte de Lucy Raitano, Rocky Swift y Kevin Buckland; Editado
en Español por Ricardo Figueroa)
 ((Mesa de edición en español;
santiago.desk@thomsonreuters.com))

headline: FOREX-Доллар падает после понижения кредитного рейтинга США
news:
ТОКИО, 19 мая (Рейтер) - Доллар идет вниз в понедельник
по отношению к ряду валют, просев до минимума 10 дней против
безопасной иены, по мере того как рынки переваривают неожиданное
ухудшение суверенного кредитного рейтинга Соединенных Штатов. 
    Индекс доллара к корзине из шести основных валют <=USD> к
16:01 МСК снизился на 0,45% до 100,3​.
    Агентство Moody's в пятницу понизило кредитный рейтинг США
на одну ступень до "Aa1", объяснив это беспокойством по поводу
госдолга, достигшего $36 триллионов.
    На фоне этих новостей доллар просел к основным соперникам
после четырех недель подъема кряду.
    "Похоже, доллар ждет новый раунд наращивания коротких
позиций после решения Moody’s. Фьючерсы на S&P500 упали на 1,2%,
и облигации США испытывают давление: на рынках идет классическая
сессия продажи американских активов", - сказал Франческо Песоле
из ING.
    Японская иена <JPY=> к доллару подорожала на 0,37%​ до
145,08, а евро <EUR=> - на 0,82% до $1,1255​. 
    Фунт стерлингов <GBP=> поднялся на 0,73% до $1,3369​.
Евросоюз и Великобритания в понедельник заключили самую
масштабную со времен Brexit двустороннюю сделку в области
торговли и обороны.
    Власти Китая в понедельник призвали Вашингтон поддержать
стабильность международной финансовой и экономической системы, а
также защитить интересы инвесторов.
    Министр финансов США Скотт Бессент сказал в телевизионном
интервью в воскресенье, что пошлины против тех торговых
партнеров, которые не захотят вести переговоры в духе доброй
воли, будут введены в тех размерах, которые объявил 2 апреля
президент Дональд Трамп.
    Между тем газета Financial Times сообщила, что США начали
серьезные переговоры с Евросоюзом, что дало некоторую надежду на
достижение торгового соглашения.
    Швейцарский франк <CHF=> укрепился на 0,42% до 0,8342​. 
    Австралийский доллар <AUD=> подорожал на 0,61% до $0,6439​
после трех дней просадки и в преддверии решения ЦБ Австралии во
вторник.
    "Киви" <NZD=> поднялся на 0,41% до $0,5905​.

    Эфириум <ETH=> вырос на 0,42% до $2.405,67.

headline: BUZZ-FX options wrap - Weak USD outlook driving price action
news:
Price action in the FX options market has been reflecting improved risk
sentiment and a more consolidative FX stance, while also recognising the threat
of more USD weakness, which was realised on Monday after the U.S. credit rating
outlook downgrade by Moody's. 
    EUR/USD and its option premiums saw the biggest rise in G10 FX. Risk
reversals were already well supported below the 5-year highs from early April
for EUR calls over puts, which flagged the topside as the more vulnerable side
of the market. The latest spot gains therefore helped EUR/USD implied volatility
extend its recovery - benchmark 1-month expiry regaining the mid 8's, having
retraced the entire post-April 2 tariff-driven gains from 7.0 to 13.0. 
    USD/JPY implied volatility showed more modest gains, having led the initial
rebound last week. Benchmark 1-month expiry reached 11.7 from a 9.5 setback low
on May 13 (16.0 was the post-April 2-tariffs high). Risk reversals remain firmly
skewed in favour USD/JPY downside over upside strikes. 
    The USD put premium is also apparent versus CHF and GBP, which highlights
the perceived vulnerability of the USD against those currencies, too. 
    USD/KRW implied volatility remains elevated and its risk reversals near
recent and multi year highs for USD puts since talk of discussions between the
two nations over FX have heightened fears of exchange rates factoring within
trade negotiations.
    Although the current bout of USD weakness may eventually revert to a
continued period of consolidation — particularly as trade dialogue continues —
the broader tone in the FX options market remains cautious. Pricing dynamics
continue to suggest that market participants are hedging for deeper, longer-term
downside risks to the USD.  
    FX options are not expecting the anticipated Reserve Bank Australia rate cut
to 3.85% on Tuesday to ignite any additional FX volatility.

headline: FOREX-Dollar retreats on US ratings downgrade; trade tensions persist
news:
* 
      Dollar dips to more than one-week low vs yen, euro, Swiss franc
    

        * 
      US trade tensions simmer, FT reports thaw with EU
    

        * 
      Bessent warns nations not negotiating 'in good faith'
    

        * 
      UK-EU defense and trade ties 'reset'
    

  
 (Adds new comment, NEW YORK dateline, byline, FX table; updates
prices)
    By Lucy Raitano and Gertrude Chavez-Dreyfuss
       LONDON/NEW YORK, May 19 (Reuters) - The U.S. dollar weakened
broadly on Monday, hitting a more than one-week low against the
safe-haven yen, Swiss franc and euro as markets digested a surprise
downgrade of the U.S. government's credit rating, while trade tensions
also weighed.
    U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said in television
interviews on Sunday that President Donald Trump will impose tariffs
at the rate he threatened last month on trading partners that do not
negotiate in "good faith".
    But Moody's action to cut the United States' top sovereign credit
rating by one notch on Friday started the ball rolling downward for
the dollar. Moody's cited concerns about the U.S. government's growing
$36 trillion debt pile.
    The move followed similar actions by Fitch in the summer of 2023,
and S&P's downgrade in 2011.    
    The news saw the dollar lose ground against its major rivals
following four straight winning weeks when it was boosted by rising
optimism for U.S. trade deals and a thaw in relations with China that
eased fears of a global recession.
    "Credit ratings matter and the fact that the U.S. sees itself
downgraded so early into the year is indicative of how negative
analysts and economists feel the impact of this new approach to trade
will be," said Juan Perez, director of trading at Monex USA in
Washington.
    "The overall financial environment remains cautious, perplexed and
on a trend of 'Sell America' which this development on credit could
further exacerbate, reflecting poorly on the dollar value going
forward."
    The greenback fell to 144.665 yen <JPY=EBS>, its lowest since May
8 on Monday, and was last down 0.4% at 145.07. It also fell to its
weakest level in more than a week at 0.8317 Swiss francs.
    The euro, meanwhile, rose 0.7% to $1.1248 <EUR=EBS>, after earlier
rising to its highest since May 9.
    Sterling <GBP=D3> also gained versus the dollar, adding 0.6% to
$1.3363. Earlier in the session the pound climbed to its highest since
April 30 as Britain agreed the most significant reset of defense and
trade ties with the European Union since Brexit on Monday. 
    Despite the dollar's losses on Monday, New York Federal Reserve
President John Williams said that he has seen no large-scale move away
from U.S. assets, and noted that the greenback remains the world's
reserve currency.
     China on Monday meanwhile called on the U.S. to take responsible
policy measures to maintain the stability of the international
financial and economic system and safeguard the interests of
investors.
    That followed Bessent's stern warning on Sunday to countries not
negotiating in good faith with the U.S. on trade.
    However, a Financial Times report that the U.S. had begun serious
trade talks with the EU brightened the mood a bit. Those talks broke a
long deadlock, offering some hope for additional deals after
Washington inked a framework agreement with Britain earlier this
month.
    Trump has previously said he has potential deals with India, Japan
and South Korea as well, although talks with Tokyo seem to be
stumbling over car tariffs.
    In the market, "there's a lot of complacency about the ability to
pull off deals," said Ray Attrill, head of FX strategy at National
Australia Bank. "Confidence that the U.S. economy is going to weather
this is very much open to question."
    Elsewhere, Trump cleared a hurdle towards passing a sweeping tax
cut bill that would add an estimated $3 trillion to $5 trillion to the
nation's debt over the next decade, after winning approval from a key
congressional committee. 
    "The focus on U.S. growth risks and the U.S. administration's

headline: FOREX-Dólar recua após rebaixamento dos EUA pela Moody's; tensões comerciais persistem
news:
Por Lucy Raitano e Gertrude Chavez-Dreyfuss
       LONDRES/NOVA YORK, 19 Mai (Reuters) - O dólar recuava
amplamente nesta segunda-feira, atingindo a mínima de mais de
uma semana ante o iene e o euro, com os mercados digerindo um
surpreendente rebaixamento da nota de crédito do governo dos
Estados Unidos, enquanto as tensões comerciais também pesavam.
    O secretário do Tesouro dos EUA, Scott Bessent, disse em
entrevistas à televisão no domingo que o presidente Donald Trump
imporá tarifas no ritmo que ameaçou no mês passado sobre os
parceiros comerciais que não negociarem de "boa fé".
    Mas a decisão da Moody's de cortar a principal nota de
crédito dos EUA em um nível na sexta-feira provocou o início da
queda do dólar. A Moody's citou preocupações sobre a crescente
dívida de US$36 trilhões do governo dos EUA.
    A medida seguiu ações semelhantes da Fitch em 2023 e da S&P
em 2011.
    A notícia fez com que o dólar perdesse terreno em relação a
seus principais pares, após quatro semanas consecutivas de
ganho, quando foi impulsionado pelo aumento do otimismo em
relação aos acordos comerciais dos EUA e por um alívio nas
tensões com a China.
    "As classificações de crédito são importantes, e o fato de
os EUA se verem rebaixados tão cedo no ano é um indicativo de
quão negativo os analistas e economistas acham que será o
impacto dessa nova abordagem ao comércio", disse Juan Perez,
diretor de negociações da Monex USA.
    "O ambiente financeiro geral continua cauteloso, perplexo e
em uma tendência de 'vender os EUA', que esse desenvolvimento no
crédito poderia exacerbar ainda mais, refletindo negativamente
no valor do dólar daqui para frente."
    O índice do dólar <=USD> -- que mede o desempenho da moeda
norte-americana frente a uma cesta de seis divisas -- caía
0,41%, a 100,350.
    O dólar tinha queda de 0,41% em relação ao iene <JPY=>, a
145,03, após atingir seu menor valor desde 8 de maio
anteriormente.
    O euro <EUR=> era negociado a US$1,124425, em alta de 0,69%
no dia, depois de subir mais cedo para seu maior valor desde 9
de maio.
     ((Tradução Redação São Paulo, +55 11 5047-3075))

headline: ОБОБЩЕНИЕ-Рубль растет с учетом геополитических надежд, скорых налогов, слабости доллара
news:
МОСКВА, 19 мая (Рейтер) - Рубль дорожает на торгах
понедельника в ожидании позитивных сигналов по итогам
сегодняшних телефонных переговоров глав США и РФ; также на
стороне российской валюты постепенное увеличение продаж
экспортной выручки под приближающийся Единый налоговый платеж. 
    В рублевых котировках доллара позитивно для российской
валюты отражается и ослабление валюты американской на форексе
после понижения суверенного кредитного рейтинга США.
    Биржевые котировки юань/рубль расчетами "завтра" к 18.00 МСК
находились вблизи отметки 11,12, рубль набирает 0,5%.
        Беспоставочные однодневные фьючерсные контракты на пары
юань/рубль, доллар/рубль, евро/рубль на Мосбирже котировались к
этому времени по 11,13, 80,80 и 90,77 соответственно, и рубль
набирает против юаня и доллара по 0,5%, а против евро дорожает
незначительно.
    Пара доллар/рубль <RUB=> котируется на форексе по 80,22,
рубль набирает 1%, согласно данным LSEG, а ранее сегодня курс
доллара опускался ниже отметки 80,00.
    Пара евро/рубль <EURRUB=> котируется на форексе по 90,28,
рубль набирает 0,1%.
    Телефонные переговоры президента США Дональда Трампа и
президента России Владимира Путина должны были начаться сегодня
в 17.00 МСК, что на выходных анонсировал глава Белого дома,
чтобы обсудить прекращение конфликта в Украине.
    Предстоящие переговоры Путина и Трампа могут подсветить
перспективы России при различных вариантах выхода из украинского
конфликта, чреватого для РФ новыми западными санкциями в случае
его продолжения.
    Сегодня же российские агентства со ссылкой на
пресс-секретаря  Кремля Дмитрия Пескова сообщили, что встреча
президентов РФ и США в настоящее время не готовится.
    Рубль остается в числе лидеров рынка форекс по темпам роста
с начала 2025 года, котируется вблизи многомесячных максимумов и
показывает положительную динамику в текущем месяце, продолжая
подпитываться надеждами на урегулирование конфликта и
нормализацию отношений между Москвой и Вашингтоном. 
    "Общая геополитическая картина для РФ сохраняет возможности
для будущей нормализации отношений с США и достижения соглашений
по Украине", - полагает Владимир Евстифеев из банка Зенит. 
    "В моменте на ожиданиях деэскалации курс способен уходить
ниже 11,10 рубля за юань, но в более долгосрочной перспективе
потенциал ослабления рубля сохраняется", - говорится в
аналитическом обзоре банка Санкт-Петербург.
    В состав проходящего 28 мая Единого налогового платежа
входит и налог на добычу полезных ископаемых (НДПИ),
уплачиваемый значительной частью экспортных компаний. Экспортеры
обычно наращивают продажи инвалюты за рубли под расчеты с
бюджетом, что обычно оказывает поддержку российской валюте во
второй половине календарного месяца.
    Согласно оценке Рейтер, объем уплачиваемого в мае
апрельского НДПИ для нефтяного сырья может составить 550
миллиардов рублей против 634 миллиардов месяцем ранее.
    Локально на стороне российской валюты играет и ослабление
внутреннего спроса на инвалюту, в том числе с учетом сокращения
импортных закупок на фоне снижения интереса населения к тратам в
пользу роста рублевых сбережений из-за высокой ключевой ставки
ЦБР (21% годовых).
    "Рубль получает традиционную порцию поддержки от ключевой
ставки и жесткой ДКП регулятора", - отмечает в этой связи Максим
Тимошенко из банка Русский Стандарт.
    На форексе валюта США значительно дешевеет после понижения
агентством Moody's суверенного кредитного рейтинга США. Индекс
доллара <=USD> снижается на 0,8% и оценивается в 100,26. В паре
с евро доллар теряет три четверти процента, текущие котировки
евро/доллар <EUR=> - $1,1250.
    По мнению Евстифеева из Зенита, глобальное ослабление
доллара и стабилизация нефтяных цен остаются факторами поддержки
для рубля.
    На прошлой неделе базовые нефтяные сорта достигли максимумов
с конца апреля, но сегодня они дешевеют после китайской
статистики, отразившей замедление в апреле темпов промышленного
производства и розничных продаж в КНР, а также на фоне снижения
кредитного рейтинга США.
    Баррель Brent <LCOc1> сейчас котируется по $65,27, теряя в
цене 0,2% с начала понедельника.
    

 (Московское бюро)
 ((moscow.newsroom@thomsonreuters.com))

headline: CORRECTED-FOREX-Dollar slips again on caution over US economy, Aussie falls after RBA
news:
(Corrects price of yen to 144.305 from 44.305 in paragraph 3;
corrects price of euro to $1.1259 from 1.1259 euros in paragraph
4; corrects analyst quote in paragraph 15, replacing summary
with full text)
    By Rocky Swift and Lucy Raitano
       TOKYO, May 20 (Reuters) - The dollar slipped on Tuesday
after declining for a week, weighed down by the Federal
Reserve's caution over the economy and as U.S. lawmakers came
closer to passing a bill expected to widen the nation's fiscal
deficit. 
    The greenback sold off broadly on Monday following last
week's downgrade of the U.S. sovereign rating by Moody's on
deficit concerns. Now attention turns to a critical vote in
Washington over U.S. President Donald Trump's sweeping tax cuts.
    Dollar selling continued on Tuesday, leaving the U.S.
currency down 0.35% against the yen at 144.305 <JPY=> hitting a
fresh 12-day low.
   The euro rose 0.14% <EUR=EBS> to $1.1259, and the Swiss franc
strengthened, pushing the dollar down 0.2% to 0.83280 francs.
    Bucking the trend was the Australian dollar which edged
lower after the Reserve Bank of Australia's cut benchmark
interest rates by 25 basis points and left the door open to
further easing in the months ahead. It was last down 0.59% to
$0.64195 <AUD=D3>, trimming a 0.8% gain on Monday.
    "Ultimately, the RBA's statement does not indicate that it
is considering pausing or ending the interest rate cycle. This
is why the AUD took a slight hit this morning," Antje Praefcke,
FX Analyst at Commerzbank, wrote in a note.
    But traders remain focused on the U.S., with Atlanta Federal
Reserve President Raphael Bostic telling CNBC on Monday the U.S.
central bank may only be able to cut interest rates by a quarter
point over the rest of the year given concerns about rising
inflation stoked by higher tariffs.
    Trump is expected to join the congressional debate over his
tax bill on Tuesday. The vote comes after Moody's stripped the
U.S. government of its top-tier credit rating, citing concerns
over the nation's growing $36.2 trillion debt pile.
    "The market is still very wary of the lack of austerity
coming from the fiscal side in the U.S." said Rodrigo Catril,
senior FX strategist at National Australia Bank.
    "We think that is potentially a driver for dollar weakness
over the coming quarters as the market is likely to demand a
higher premium to lend money to the U.S.," he added.
    Trump's bill would add $3 trillion to $5 trillion to the
debt, according to nonpartisan analysts. Ballooning fiscal debt,
trade frictions, and weakened confidence have weighed on U.S.
assets. The U.S. dollar index has tumbled as much as 10.6% from
its January highs, one of the sharpest retreats for a
three-month period.
    The dollar got a breather after Trump paused many of the
largest tariffs he announced last month. But comments from
Japan's top trade envoy on Tuesday that Tokyo was firm in its
anti-tariff stance pointed to no easy off-ramp in the
negotiations in the weeks and months ahead.
    And in the wake of Trump's tariff turmoil, Britain on Monday
agreed to the most significant reset of defence and trade ties
with the European Union since Brexit 
    The pound was last up 0.16% at 1.33840 <GBP=D3> having risen
0.6% on Monday.
    "Optimism surrounding key UK economic data and a major
political breakthrough has fuelled sterling’s gains alongside
broad-based dollar weakness," wrote George Vessey, lead FX and
macro strategist at Convera.
    Elsewhere, the Chinese yuan weakened against the as China
cut key benchmark lending rates while corporate seasonal demand
for dollars remained high. 

 (Reporting by Lucy Raitano and Rocky Swift; Editing by Stephen
Coates and David Evans)

headline: 更正-《全球汇市》对美国经济的谨慎态度令美元续跌，央行降息后澳元下跌
news:
(因英文原文有误，更正内文倒数第二段分析师引语)
       路透东京5月20日 - 美元在连续一周走低后周二继续下滑，因美
联储对经济持谨慎态度，以及美国议员更接近通过一项可能导致国家财政
赤字扩大的法案。
    
    上周评级机构穆迪（Moody's）因财政赤字问题意外下调了美国主权
评级后，美元在周一全线下滑。现在，人们的注意力转向美国国会，议员
们即将就特朗普总统的全面减税法案进行关键的投票。[nL6S3RR11D]
    
    周二美元继续遭到抛售，导致美元兑日圆<JPY=>下跌0.35%，报144.3
05日圆，创下12天来的新低。
    
    欧元兑美元 <EUR=EBS> 上涨0.14% 至 1.1259美元，瑞郎走强，推动
美元兑瑞郎下跌 0.2% 至 0.83280 瑞郎。
    
    澳元兑美元逆势下跌，因此前澳洲央行将指标利率下调 25 个基点，
并为未来几个月进一步放松政策敞开了大门。澳元兑美元<AUD=D3>最新下
跌0.59%，至0.64195美元，周一为上涨0.8%。
    
    “最终，澳洲央行的声明并未表明其正在考虑暂停或结束降息周期。
这是澳元今早小幅下跌的原因，”德国商业银行外汇分析师 Antje Praef
cke 在一份报告中写道。
    
    但交易员们的焦点仍在美国，亚特兰大联储总裁博斯蒂克周一对CNBC
表示，鉴于进口税提高可能引发通胀上升的担忧，美联储在今年剩余时间
内可能只能降息25个基点。[nL6S3RR0Y6]
    
    预计特朗普周二将参加国会对其全面减税法案的辩论。
    
    澳洲国民银行高级外汇策略师Rodrigo Catril表示："市场对美国财
政方面缺乏撙节仍然非常警惕。"
    
    他补充说："我们认为，这可能是未来几个季度驱动美元走软的一个
潜在因素，因为市场对于将资金借贷给美国可能会要求更高的溢价。"
    
    据无党派分析人士称，特朗普的税改法案将使政府债务增加3万亿至5
万亿美元。不断膨胀的财政债务、贸易摩擦以及对美国例外论的信心减弱
，都对美国资产造成了压力。美元指数已从1月高点下跌多达10.6%，创下
最大的三个月跌幅。
    
    在特朗普暂停了他上月宣布的许多高额关税之后，美元得到了喘息的
机会。但日本最高贸易特使周二表示，日方要求美国取消关税的立场没有
改变。这表明未来的谈判不会轻易结束。[nL6S3RR06D]
    
    在特朗普的关税引发动荡之后，英国周一同意与欧盟重启自英国脱欧

headline: FOREX-Dólar recua novamente com cautela sobre economia dos EUA
news:
Por Rocky Swift e Lucy Raitano
       TÓQUIO, 20 Mai (Reuters) - O dólar recuava novamente
nesta terça-feira, depois de cair na véspera, pressionado pela
cautela do Federal Reserve em relação à economia dos Estados
Unidos e com os parlamentares norte-americanos chegando mais
perto de aprovar um projeto de lei que deve aumentar o déficit
fiscal do país.
    O dólar foi amplamente vendido na segunda-feira, após o
rebaixamento da nota de crédito dos Estados Unidos pela agência
Moody's na semana passada, devido a preocupações com o déficit. 
    Agora, as atenções se voltam para uma votação crítica no
Congresso sobre os cortes abrangentes de impostos do presidente
dos EUA, Donald Trump.
    O índice do dólar <=USD> -- que mede o desempenho da moeda
norte-americana frente a uma cesta de seis divisas -- caía
0,13%, a 100,300.
    O dólar tinha queda de 0,2% em relação ao iene <JPY=>, a
144,56. 
    O euro <EUR=> era negociado a US$1,1247, em alta de 0,03% no
dia.
    Os investidores continuam concentrados nos EUA, com o
presidente do Federal Reserve de Atlanta, Raphael Bostic,
dizendo à CNBC na segunda-feira que o banco central talvez só
consiga cortar a taxa de juros em 0,25 ponto percentual até o
fim do ano, devido às preocupações com o aumento da inflação.
    Espera-se que Trump participe do debate no Congresso sobre
sua legislação tributária na terça-feira. A votação ocorre
depois que a Moody's retirou do governo dos EUA sua maior nota
de crédito, citando preocupações com a crescente dívida de
US$36,2 trilhões do país.
    "O mercado ainda está muito cauteloso com a falta de
austeridade vinda do lado fiscal dos EUA", disse Rodrigo Catril,
estrategista sênior de câmbio do National Australia Bank.
    "Acreditamos que isso seja potencialmente um fator de
fraqueza do dólar nos próximos trimestres, já que o mercado
provavelmente exigirá um prêmio maior para emprestar dinheiro
aos EUA", acrescentou.

headline: FOREX-Dollar slips on caution over US economy, traders mull US-Japan talks
news:
(Updates price moves, adds strategist quote in para 3, 6 and 7,
adds news on US-Japan talks in para 5, moves euro and franc to
para 19, moves Chinese yuan to para 10)
    By Lucy Raitano and Rocky Swift
       TOKYO, May 20 (Reuters) - The dollar slipped again on
Tuesday after declining for a week, weighed down by the Federal
Reserve's caution over the economy while traders considered news
that upcoming U.S.-Japan talks could include discussions on FX
and avoiding volatility. 
    The greenback sold off broadly on Monday following last
week's downgrade of the U.S. sovereign rating by Moody's on
deficit concerns. Now attention turns to a critical vote in
Washington over U.S. President Donald Trump's sweeping tax cuts.
    "We’ve got a bit of a hangover from the Moody’s story and
what it means for the dollar in general. We still think there is
risk premium embedded in the dollar," said Chris Turner, head of
FX strategy at ING.    
    The U.S. currency was softer against the yen, last down 0.2%
at 144.510 <JPY=>, having hit a fresh 12-day low earlier in the
session. 
    On traders' radar is news around upcoming U.S.-Japan talks,
with Japanese Finance Minister Katsunobu Kato saying on Tuesday
he expects any bilateral meeting with U.S. Treasury Secretary
Scott Bessent on exchange rates to be based on their shared view
that excessive currency volatility was undesirable.
    Kato and Bessent are expected to hold a bilateral meeting on
the sidelines of a G7 finance leaders' gathering to be held this
week in Canada. 
    "Overhanging the FX market is that discussions in trade
deals are going to include some currency component, which if it
does is a dollar negative, because the U.S. wants a weaker
dollar against Asian currencies to narrow the Asian trade
surplus with the States," said ING's Turner. 
    Elsewhere, the Australian dollar edged lower after the
Reserve Bank of Australia cut benchmark interest rates by 25
basis points and left the door open to further easing in the
months ahead. It was last down 0.68% to $0.64135 <AUD=D3>,
trimming a 0.8% gain on Monday.
    "Ultimately, the RBA's statement does not indicate that it
is considering pausing or ending the interest rate cycle. This
is why the AUD took a slight hit this morning," Antje Praefcke,
FX Analyst at Commerzbank, wrote in a note.
    Meanwhile the Chinese yuan weakened against the dollar as
China cut key benchmark lending rates while corporate seasonal
demand for dollars remained high. 
    But traders remain focused on the U.S., with Atlanta Federal
Reserve President Raphael Bostic telling CNBC on Monday the U.S.
central bank may only be able to cut interest rates by a quarter
point over the rest of the year given concerns about rising
inflation stoked by higher tariffs.
    Trump is expected to join the congressional debate over his
tax bill on Tuesday. The vote comes after Moody's stripped the
U.S. government of its top-tier credit rating, citing concerns
over the nation's growing $36.2 trillion debt pile.
    "The market is still very wary of the lack of austerity
coming from the fiscal side in the U.S." said Rodrigo Catril,
senior FX strategist at National Australia Bank.
    "We think that is potentially a driver for dollar weakness
over the coming quarters as the market is likely to demand a
higher premium to lend money to the U.S.," he added.
    Trump's bill would add $3 trillion to $5 trillion to the
debt, according to nonpartisan analysts. Ballooning fiscal debt,
trade frictions, and weakened confidence have weighed on U.S.
assets. The U.S. dollar index has tumbled as much as 10.6% from
its January highs, one of the sharpest retreats for a
three-month period.
    The dollar got a breather after Trump paused many of the
largest tariffs he announced last month. But comments from
Japan's top trade envoy on Tuesday that Tokyo was firm in its
anti-tariff stance pointed to no easy off-ramp in the
negotiations in the weeks and months ahead.
    And in the wake of Trump's tariff turmoil, Britain on Monday
agreed to the most significant reset of defence and trade ties
with the European Union since Brexit 
    The pound was flat at 1.33620 <GBP=D3> having risen 0.6% on
Monday.
    "Optimism surrounding key UK economic data and a major
political breakthrough has fuelled sterling’s gains alongside
broad-based dollar weakness," wrote George Vessey, lead FX and
macro strategist at Convera.
    The euro was also flat <EUR=EBS> at $1.124550, and the Swiss
franc strengthened, pushing the dollar down 0.1% to 0.83360
francs.

 (Reporting by Lucy Raitano and Rocky Swift; Editing by Stephen
Coates, David Evans, Alexandra Hudson)

headline: FOREX-El dólar cae por cautela sobre economía EEUU, negociaciones entre Washington y Tokio
news:
Por Lucy Raitano y Rocky Swift
       TOKIO, 20 mayo (Reuters) - El dólar volvía a caer el
martes tras una semana a la baja, lastrado por la cautela de la
Reserva Federal sobre la economía, mientras los operadores
consideraban las noticias de que las próximas conversaciones
entre Estados Unidos y Japón podrían incluir discusiones sobre
divisas y evitar la volatilidad.
    * El billete verde se vendió ampliamente el lunes tras la
rebaja de la calificación soberana de Estados Unidos por parte
de Moody's la semana pasada, debido a la preocupación por el
déficit. Ahora la atención se centra en una votación crítica en
Washington sobre los amplios recortes de impuestos del
presidente estadounidense Donald Trump.
    * La divisa estadounidense se debilitaba frente al yen, con
una caída del 0,2%, a 144,510 <JPY=>, tras haber alcanzado un
nuevo mínimo de 12 días a comienzos de la sesión.
    * El martes, el ministro japonés de Finanzas, Katsunobu
Kato, declaró que espera que cualquier reunión bilateral con el
secretario del Tesoro estadounidense, Scott Bessent, sobre los
tipos de cambio se base en la opinión compartida de que no es
deseable una excesiva volatilidad de las divisas.
    * Por otra parte, el dólar australiano bajaba después de que
el Banco de la Reserva de Australia recortó las tasas de interés
de referencia en 25 puntos básicos y dejó la puerta abierta a
una mayor relajación en los próximos meses. La moneda <AUD=D3>
caía un 0,68%, a 0,64135 dólares estadounidenses, tras recortar
la subida del 0,8% registrada el lunes.
    * Por su parte, el yuan chino se debilitaba frente al dólar,
ya que China recortó las tasas de interés de referencia,
mientras que la demanda estacional de dólares por parte de las
empresas se mantuvo elevada.
    * Pero los operadores siguen centrados en Estados Unidos,
con el presidente de la Reserva Federal de Atlanta, Raphael
Bostic, diciendo a CNBC el lunes que el banco central de Estados
Unidos sólo podrá recortar las tasas de interés en un cuarto de
punto en lo que queda de año, dadas las preocupaciones sobre el
aumento de la inflación avivada por los aranceles.
    * Se espera que Trump se incorpore el martes al debate en el
Congreso sobre su proyecto de ley fiscal. La votación se produce
después de que Moody's despojó al gobierno de Estados Unidos de
su calificación crediticia de primer nivel, citando
preocupaciones sobre la creciente deuda de 36,2 billones de
dólares de la nación.
    * El proyecto de ley de Trump añadiría entre 3 billones y 5
billones de dólares a la deuda, según analistas no partidistas.
La abultada deuda fiscal, las fricciones comerciales y el
debilitamiento de la confianza han lastrado los activos
estadounidenses. El índice del dólar se ha desplomado hasta un
10,6% desde sus máximos de enero, uno de los retrocesos más
pronunciados en un periodo de tres meses.
    * La libra <GBP=D3> operaba plana a 1,33620 dólares tras
haber subido un 0,6% el lunes.
    * El euro <EUR=EBS> también cotizaba plano a 1,124550
dólares, y el franco suizo se fortalecía, haciendo caer al dólar
un 0,1% a 0,83360 francos.

 (Reporte de Lucy Raitano y Rocky Swift; Editado en Español por
Ricardo Figueroa)

santiago.desk@thomsonreuters.com))

headline: Рубль стоек на FX и слаб на MOEX после общения Путина и Трампа, санкций Евросоюза
news:
МОСКВА, 20 мая (Рейтер) - Рубль сохраняет смешанную
динамику на дневных торгах вторника, стремясь к росту на форексе
и дешевея на локальном рынке, что может быть вызвано более
оптимистичным отношением внешних игроков к итогам вчерашних
переговоров глав США и РФ, но достаточно скептическим - со
стороны российских участников.
    Свою роль в негативной динамике рубля на Мосбирже может
играть факт принятия Евросоюзом 17-го пакета санкций против РФ,
в том числе против теневого флота, перевозящего российскую
нефть, что чревато снижением притока экспортной валютной выручки
в Россию.
    Не в пользу рубля также и отсутствие пока повышенных продаж
инвалюты экспортерами под предстоящие в следующую среду
налоговые выплаты.
    Биржевые котировки юань/рубль расчетами "завтра" к 15.00 МСК
находились вблизи отметки 11,19, и рубль дешевеет на 1%, ранее
слабея до недельного минимума 11,24.
        Беспоставочные однодневные фьючерсные контракты на пары
юань/рубль, доллар/рубль, евро/рубль на Мосбирже котировались к
этому времени по 11,20, 81,20 и 91,40 соответственно, и рубль
теряет против юаня 1%, против доллара - 0,9%, против евро
дешевеет на 1%.
    Пара доллар/рубль <RUB=> котируется на форексе по 80,55,
рубль набирает 0,2%, согласно данным LSEG, утром дорожая до
79,50, что было совсем близко от достигнутого неделю назад почти
двухлетнего максимума российской валюты, 79,37 за доллар.
    Пара евро/рубль <EURRUB=> котируется на форексе по 90,40,
рубль набирает 0,4%.
    По итогам вчерашнего телефонного разговора глав США и РФ
американский президент Дональд Трамп сказал, что Москва и Киев
"немедленно начнут переговоры" о прекращении огня, отметив при
этом - "тон и дух беседы были превосходными", а Россия хочет
вести "крупномасштабную" торговлю со Штатами после окончания
конфликта.
    В свою очередь российский президент Владимир Путин после
этого разговора сказал, что Москва выступает за мирное
урегулирование украинского кризиса и готова работать с
украинской стороной над меморандумом по поводу возможного
будущего мирного договора.
    "Телефонный разговор Трампа и Путина не принес конкретики в
урегулировании украинского кризиса, но подтверждает сохранение
базы для дальнейших переговоров", - сказала Елена Кожухова из
компании Велес Капитал, предположив, что США на данный момент,
похоже, не собираются вводить новые санкции против РФ и готовы
продолжать диалог.
    "Ему (рублю) продолжат оказывать поддержку и ситуация на
рынке энергоносителей, где ближайший фьючерс на нефть марки
Brent удерживает позиции выше $65 долларов за баррель Brent,
слабый спрос на валюту со стороны импортеров на фоне высоких
ставок в экономике, а также постепенная активизация продаж
иностранной валюты со стороны экспортеров в преддверии пика
налоговых выплат", - считает Богдан Зварич из ПСБ.
    В состав проходящего 28 мая Единого налогового платежа
входит налог на добычу полезных ископаемых, и согласно оценке
Рейтер, объем уплачиваемого в мае апрельского НДПИ для нефтяного
сырья может составить 550 миллиардов рублей.
    Локально на стороне российской валюты играет и ослабление
внутреннего спроса на инвалюту, в том числе с учетом сокращения
импортных закупок на фоне снижения интереса населения к тратам в
пользу роста рублевых сбережений из-за высокой ключевой ставки
ЦБР (21% годовых).
    При этом большинство аналитиков сходятся во мнении, что
рубль переоценен. В последнем опросе Рейтер экономисты
прогнозируют курс доллара в 95 рублей через 12 месяцев.
Американский банк Goldman Sachs прогнозирует, что рубль вернется
к отметке 100 за доллар уже к середине лета.

news:

рейтинга США агентством Moody's. Теперь внимание переключилось

headline: BUZZ-FX options wrap - USD warnings, hedging flows, Asia FX risks
news:
FX option implied volatility has turned more negatively correlated with the USD,
consequently easing from Monday's highs as the recent dollar decline pauses.
However, implied volatility remains well above last week's pullback lows,
underscoring the ongoing uncertainty and potential FX risks that lie ahead.  
    Risk reversals are a key gauge of directional risk in FX markets, reflecting
the implied volatility premium dealers assign to strikes on the side they
perceive as more vulnerable or prone to greater price swings. For many
currencies, that premium is for USD weakness. 
    EUR/USD risk reversals have been trading their highest EUR call/USD put risk
premiums since 2020, while GBP/USD risk reversals have reached their highest
premiums for GBP calls/USD puts since the financial crisis. 
    USD/JPY risk reversals maintain a solid JPY call/USD put premium, albeit
below its most recent highs, but there's also been continued demand to hedge the
risk of deeper declines with outright JPY call/USD put options. 
    Part of the reason for the JPY call/USD put demand is due to the fear that
foreign exchange rates may be used as a trade negotiating tool between the U.S.
and some Asian countries. Those fears were heightened after it emerged that the
U.S. and South Korea had spoken about FX in early May, fuelling demand and
premiums for USD/KWN options, with USD puts once again at the fore.
